svg.text: FIGURE 3: GRAPH THEORY, TOPOLOGICAL MATRICES & TELLEGEN PROOF ENGINE
Oriented Graphs, Trees & Co-Trees, Incidence, Fundamental Cut-Set, Fundamental Tie-Set & Dual Matrix Orthogonalities

g.text: 1. Oriented Graph & Tree Topology
Graph Abstraction & Elements
• Linear Graph G = (V, E) replaces electrical components with lines
connecting junctions (nodes n, branches b).
• Oriented Graph: Every branch has an assigned arrow indicating reference current direction.
• Connected Graph: Path exists between every pair of nodes (k = 1 subgraphs).
• Planar Graph: Can be drawn on a 2D plane without any crossing branches.
• Non-Planar: Cannot be drawn without crossings (Mesh analysis FAILS!).
Tree & Co-Tree Mathematical Definition
• A Tree (T) is a connected subgraph of G that:
1. Contains ALL n nodes of the original graph.
2. Contains NO closed loops (acyclic graph).
Fundamental Dimension Invariants:
Tree Branches (Twigs) = n - 1
Co-Tree Branches (Links / Chords) l = b - (n - 1) = b - n + 1
• Co-Tree (T*): The set of all links remaining when twigs are removed.
• Twig properties: Every twig connects 2 nodes. Removing any 1 twig splits tree into 2 subtrees!
• Link properties: Adding any 1 link to a tree forms EXACTLY ONE closed fundamental loop!
• Rank of Graph: r = n - 1. Nullity of Graph: μ = b - n + 1.
Enumeration of Trees: Cayley & Binet-Cauchy
• Complete Graph K_n (every pair of nodes connected by an edge):
Total Trees T(K_n) = n^(n - 2)
For n = 3: 3¹ = 3 trees | For n = 4: 4² = 16 trees | For n = 5: 5³ = 125 trees!
General Graph Matrix Tree Theorem (Laplacian / Admittance):
Total Trees N_T = det( A · A^T )
where A is the Reduced Incidence Matrix of size (n-1) × b!
• Every non-singular submatrix of A of order (n-1) corresponds to a unique valid tree.
★ Determinant of any tree submatrix in A is always either +1 or -1 (unimodular!).
GATE Exam Quick-Check Tree Rules
To test whether a given set of branches forms a valid Tree:
1. Count test: Must contain EXACTLY n - 1 branches. (If ≠ n-1, REJECT!).
2. Acyclic test: Must NOT contain any closed loop. (If loop exists, REJECT!).
3. Connectivity test: Must connect ALL n nodes together.
Example: For n=4, b=6 (Bridge circuit), n-1 = 3 twigs.
Total combinations C(6, 3) = 20. Closed triangles = 4.
Valid trees = 20 - 4 = 16 trees! det(A A^T) = 16.
2. Incidence Matrix & KCL Formulation
Complete Incidence Matrix A_a [Order n × b]
• Describes connection between nodes and branches:
a_ij = +1 if branch j leaves node i
a_ij = -1 if branch j enters node i
a_ij = 0 if branch j is not connected to node i
Fundamental Structural Properties of A_a:
1. Each column has exactly ONE +1 and ONE -1 (since each branch connects 2 nodes).
2. Sum of elements in ANY column is ZERO: ∑_i a_ij = 0.
3. Rows of A_a are linearly dependent! Rank(A_a) = n - 1 < n.
Reduced Incidence Matrix A [Order (n-1) × b]
• Obtained by deleting ANY ONE row (the reference/datum node):
Rank(A) = n - 1 (Full Row Rank!)
• Partitioning A into Twigs (A_t) and Links (A_l):
A = [ A_t | A_l ]
where A_t is a non-singular square matrix of size (n-1) × (n-1), det(A_t) = ±1.
Matrix Form of Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL):
A · i_b = 0 [where i_b = (b × 1) branch currents]
Represents n - 1 linearly independent KCL equations!
Branch Voltages in Terms of Node Voltages
• Let v_n be the (n-1) × 1 vector of node-to-datum potentials.
• The b × 1 branch voltage vector v_b is given by the TRANSPOSE of A:
v_b = A^T · v_n
Component Expansion for Branch k from Node i to j:
v_b,k = v_n,i - v_n,j
• If terminal j is the datum node (v_n,j = 0): v_b,k = v_n,i.
• Guarantees that KVL is satisfied automatically across every loop!
• Fundamental relation connecting node analysis directly to branch analysis.
Systematic Node Admittance Matrix Formulation
• Branch Constitutive Law: i_b = Y_b · v_b - I_s
• Multiplying by Reduced Incidence Matrix A:
A · i_b = A · Y_b · (A^T · v_n) - A · I_s = 0
( A · Y_b · A^T ) · v_n = A · I_s
• Node Admittance Matrix: Y_node = A · Y_b · A^T (symmetric & positive definite!).
• Source Injection Vector: I_node = A · I_s (net currents entering nodes).
3. Fundamental Tie-Set Matrix & KVL
Fundamental Loop (f-loop / Tie-Set) Concept
• For a given tree T, adding ONE link forms exactly ONE closed path (f-loop).
• An f-loop contains EXACTLY ONE link and one or more twigs.
• Number of Fundamental Tie-Sets: l = b - n + 1.
• The orientation of the f-loop is chosen IDENTICAL to the orientation of its defining link!
Tie-Set Matrix Definition B_f [Order (b-n+1) × b]:
b_ij = +1 if branch j direction aligns with loop i
b_ij = -1 if branch j direction opposes loop i
b_ij = 0 if branch j is not present in loop i
Canonical Partitioning of B_f
• Order branches such that Twigs are listed first, Links second:
B_f = [ B_t | I_l ]
• I_l is an IDENTITY matrix of order l × l = (b-n+1) × (b-n+1).
• B_t is a submatrix of order (b-n+1) × (n-1) containing twig entries.
Rank of Fundamental Tie-Set Matrix:
Rank(B_f) = b - n + 1 (Full Row Rank!)
• Proves all l fundamental loop equations are mutually linearly independent!
Matrix Form of Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL)
• Along any closed fundamental loop, algebraic sum of branch voltages is ZERO:
B_f · v_b = 0
• Expanding by partitions [ B_t | I_l ] · [ v_t ; v_l ] = 0:
B_t · v_t + v_l = 0 ⇒ v_l = - B_t · v_t
• Link voltages are COMPLETELY DETERMINED by twig voltages!
Branch Currents from Loop Currents:
i_b = B_f^T · i_l
where i_l is the (b-n+1) × 1 vector of fundamental link currents.
Systematic Mesh Impedance Matrix Formulation
• Branch Constitutive Law: v_b = Z_b · i_b - V_s
• Multiplying by Fundamental Tie-Set Matrix B_f:
B_f · v_b = B_f · Z_b · (B_f^T · i_l) - B_f · V_s = 0
( B_f · Z_b · B_f^T ) · i_l = B_f · V_s
• Mesh Impedance Matrix: Z_mesh = B_f · Z_b · B_f^T (symmetric & positive definite!).
• Source Voltage Vector: V_mesh = B_f · V_s (net clockwise loop driving voltages).
4. Cut-Set Matrix & Grand Orthogonality
Fundamental Cut-Set (f-cutset) Concept
• A Cut-Set is a minimal set of branches whose removal divides graph into 2 parts.
• An f-cutset contains EXACTLY ONE twig and one or more links.
• Number of Fundamental Cut-Sets: n - 1 (equal to number of twigs!).
• The orientation of an f-cutset is chosen IDENTICAL to the defining twig!
Canonical Partitioning of Q_f [Order (n-1) × b]:
Q_f = [ I_t | Q_l ]
• I_t is an IDENTITY matrix of order (n-1) × (n-1) representing the twigs.
• Q_l is an (n-1) × (b-n+1) matrix representing link incidence in cutsets.
The Grand Matrix Orthogonality Theorems
Theorem 1: Incidence & Tie-Set Orthogonality:
A · B_f^T ≡ 0 ⟺ B_f · A^T ≡ 0
Every loop enters and leaves any cut surface equal number of times!
Theorem 2: Cut-Set & Tie-Set Orthogonality:
Q_f · B_f^T ≡ 0 ⟺ B_f · Q_f^T ≡ 0
Proof via Matrix Multiplication:
[ I_t | Q_l ] · [ B_t^T ; I_l ] = B_t^T + Q_l ≡ 0
Q_l = - B_t^T ⟺ B_t = - Q_l^T
Topological Proof of Tellegen's Law
• Total network power absorbed across all b branches:
P = v_b^T · i_b = ∑_(k=1)^b v_k · i_k
Proof 1 (Via Node Potentials & KCL):
Substitute branch voltages v_b = A^T · v_n:
P = ( A^T · v_n )^T · i_b = v_n^T · ( A · i_b )
Since KCL states A · i_b = 0 ⇒ P = v_n^T · 0 ≡ 0 !
Proof 2 (Via Loop Currents & KVL):
Substitute branch currents i_b = B_f^T · i_l:
P = v_b^T · ( B_f^T · i_l ) = ( B_f · v_b )^T · i_l
Since KVL states B_f · v_b = 0 ⇒ P = 0^T · i_l ≡ 0 !
Master Graph Theory Invariants Summary
• Twigs = n - 1 | Links l = b - n + 1 | Branches b = Twigs + Links.
• Rank of Complete Incidence Matrix: Rank(A_a) = n - 1.
• Rank of Reduced Incidence Matrix: Rank(A) = n - 1.
• Rank of Tie-Set Matrix: Rank(B_f) = b - n + 1.
• Rank of Cut-Set Matrix: Rank(Q_f) = n - 1.
• Trees in Complete Graph K_n: T = n^(n - 2).
• Trees in General Graph: T = det(A A^T) = det(Q_f Q_f^T).
